div.head: Ine 50
div.ab: XCIIII. Gif gesiðcund mon ðingaþ wið cyning oþþe wið his ealdermon for his innhiwum oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oþþe for frige, nah he þær nan witerædene, se gesiþ, forþonðe he him nolde ǽr yfles gestyran æt ham.

XCIIII. Gif gesiðcund mon þingað wið cyning oððe wið kyninges ealdormonnan for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he þær nane witerædenne, se gesið, forðon he him nolde ær yfles gestieran æt ham.

Si homo siþcundus agat cum rege uel cum regis aldermanno pro familia sua uel cum domino suo pro seruo uel libero, non habeat ibi aliquam wite redditionem ea uice, quia noluit eos prius a malo castigare domi.

{XCIIII} Gif gesiðcund man þingað wið cyning oððe wið kyninges ealdormonnan for his inhiwan oððe wið his hlaford for ðeowe oððe for frige, nah he þær nane witerædenne, se gesið, forðon he him nolde ær yfles gestieran æt ham.

If a nobly born man settles with the king or with the king’s ealdorman on behalf of [a member of] his household, or with his lord on behalf of a slave or a free man, the nobleman does not receive any portion of the fine, because he was unable earlier to restrain him at home from wrongdoing.

If a nobleman comes to terms with the king, or with the king's ealdorman, or with his lord, on behalf of his dependants, free or unfree, he, the nobleman, shall not have any portion of the fines, because he has not previously taken care at home to restrain them [his men] from evil doing.

Wenn ein Mann vom Gefolgschaftsstande gegenüber dem König oder dem königlichen Ealdorman für seine Gutsinsassen oder gegenüber seinem Herrn für unfreie oder freie [Schutzbefohlene eine Schuldsühne] abmacht, so erhält er, der Gefolgsmann, nun keinen Antheil am Strafgelde, weil er damals zu Hause ihn [den Schuldigen] an [dessen] Missethat zu hindern unterlassen hat.

If a man of the retainer class makes [a settlement for an offence] with the king or with the king’s ealdorman on behalf of his household, or with his lord on behalf of unfree or free [dependants], then he, the retainer, gets no share of the fine, because he failed at the time to restrain him [the guilty man] from [his] misdeed at home.
